h: Out at the far end of Sheppey
p: Leysdown-on-Sea is right at the eastern tip of the Isle of Sheppey, a classic Kent seaside resort ringed by caravan and holiday parks. It's a long drive across the island from the Sheppey Crossing, so most people come here for the day or stay on one of the parks. Like most seaside arcades, it keeps the cash-prize machines in a separate 18+ area, so check the signs as you go in.

Away from the promenade, the coast past Leysdown gets wild and quiet very quickly. The Swale National Nature Reserve at Shellness is great for birdwatching, and Elmley National Nature Reserve on the island is another good bet for wildlife. Back on the prom, there's no shortage of chips, ice cream and seaside cafés.
